title: Wheels Win? Rolling Friction Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A suitcase on wheels glides with one finger, while a steel cupboard just as heavy needs two people to drag. Why does rolling make heavy things so easy? And why does Aarav's bicycle feel like it is climbing a hill on a level road, the moment his back tyre goes flat? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn rolling friction: the force that opposes rolling.

On a live motion notebook one box is dragged across a rough floor, then put on a light trolley, with loads of 50, 75 and 100 kg. The readout and a force vs load graph move together: 196 N, 294 N and 392 N to keep it sliding, but only 4.9 N to 9.8 N on wheels. A slow-mo replay looks under one wheel: the floor and the tyre squash into a small patch, and the floor's push leans backwards. We build f_k = mu_k N and f_r = mu_r N step by step, follow the flat tyre link by link, compare scraping with rolling, see why friction is also needed for walking, cycling and braking, and how oil and ball bearings cut wasted friction. Then a worked example on a railway wagon, the exam trap, and an original JEE Main pattern question.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
